nominees.name: Rob Sand
team: Running mate: Dave Muhlbauer, Crawford County supervisor (Wikipedia, 2026 Iowa elections).

positions.stance: End private management (MCOs) of Iowa Medicaid, paying providers directly through a state-run nonprofit-style system; would sign the Work Without Worry bill lifting Medicaid income/asset limits for working Iowans with disabilities.
State board to negotiate prescription drug prices; cap utility fees; expand surprise medical billing law; $2,000 family caregiver tax credit.
Universal free preschool and school lunches; income limits, tuition-increase caps and annual audits for private-school tuition assistance.
Cut state regulation and simplify permitting to encourage homebuilding.
Floated marijuana-legalization tax revenue and higher taxes on data centers as possible funding for Medicaid changes.

policyShifts.shift: Reverse the managed-care model: a move from private MCOs to state direct payment. This reshapes Iowa HHS procurement, contracts and provider payment systems.
New state drug-price negotiation board and utility fee caps would require new statutory authority and standing up a board and staff.
Universal free preschool and school lunches would add recurring state costs; guardrails on private school tuition assistance would amend the existing program.
Regulatory simplification and permitting reform could be partly administrative (state rules) and partly statutory.

impediments.title: Republican legislature
impediments.detail: Republicans hold a House supermajority and a Senate majority; Sand says he expects to work with them. Most of his agenda needs legislation.

impediments.title: Funding gaps
impediments.detail: Reporting found no price tags or funding sources for his proposals, and direct Medicaid payment could cost the state more.

impediments.title: Medicaid transition risk
impediments.detail: Sand himself says reversing privatization will take time and must be done carefully to avoid failure.

impediments.title: Tax-revenue assumptions
impediments.detail: Marijuana-legalization revenue and higher data-center taxes depend on legislative action that Republican leaders are unlikely to take quickly (inference).

insights: First Democratic governor since Culver in 2011 if the result stands; cabinet-level turnover is likely large because all current directors were appointed by Reynolds (inference; verify).
Sand is State Auditor, so an auditor-office staff pipeline and budget-oversight experience are plausible sources of senior hires (inference).

analysis.assumption: Scenario: assumes Rob Sand wins the Nov. 3, 2026 general election. AP lookup shows the race called (Nov. 4, 2026 04:34 UTC); this tool does not make calls. Not a call or forecast.
analysis.summary: Sand would be a Democratic governor facing a Republican House supermajority and Senate majority, so his agenda splits into administrative actions (Medicaid contract strategy, appointments, procurement) and legislative asks that need Republican votes. His Medicaid privatization reversal is the largest operational and procurement event.
analysis.timing: Inauguration expected mid-January 2027 (verify date); first budget and Medicaid contract decisions in the first session.
firstMoves: Name chief of staff and Iowa HHS/Medicaid leadership.
Open talks with Republican leaders on Work Without Worry, which had bipartisan support.
Review MCO contracts for exit timing.
